questions.question: What does a BI Developer / Analytics Engineer primarily own?
options: The data pipelines and warehouse infrastructure
The semantic layer between raw data and business decisions — model, calculations, dashboards, last-mile quality
The machine-learning models and feature engineering
The cloud networking and IAM policies
questions.explanation: The BI developer owns the semantic layer; pipelines are the Data Engineer's, ML is the Data Scientist's.

questions.question: In the analytics maturity model, where does most BI work sit?
questions.explanation: BI lives mainly in descriptive (what happened) and diagnostic (why); a good model enables the rest downstream.

questions.question: What does 'audience first, tool second' mean?
options: Pick the newest visual, then find an audience for it
Decide who the audience is and what decision/action follows before choosing a chart type
Always use Power BI regardless of the audience
Let the data source dictate the design
questions.explanation: Design starts from the audience and the decision to be enabled — the tool and chart type come after.

questions.question: What is the 'five-second test'?
options: A dashboard must load in five seconds
A new user should grasp a page's main insight within five seconds
You have five seconds to pitch to a VP
Refresh must complete in five seconds
questions.explanation: If a viewer can't get the main insight in ~5 seconds, the page needs redesigning.

questions.question: How many weighted dimensions does the recruitment rubric use?
questions.explanation: Six: Design & UX (25), DAX (20), Modeling (20), KPI (15), Enterprise BI (10), Communication (10).

questions.question: Why is a star schema preferred over a fully normalized model for BI?
options: Fewer joins, better compression, faster and simpler queries for the calc engine
It removes the need for a Date table
questions.explanation: Star schemas are optimized for analytics; normalization suits OLTP, not BI.

questions.question: What does the 'grain' of a fact table define?
options: The level of detail one row represents
questions.explanation: Grain is what one fact row means (one transaction, one daily snapshot). Every measure depends on it.

questions.question: A fact has OrderDate and ShipDate against one Date table. How do you report on both?
options: Duplicate the Date table twice and hide one
Use a role-playing dimension: one active relationship + USERELATIONSHIP for the inactive one
questions.explanation: Only one relationship can be active; activate the other inside CALCULATE with USERELATIONSHIP.

questions.question: When is bidirectional cross-filtering justified?
options: Always — it is the safe default
When you must filter a dimension by the fact (e.g., a slicer showing only used values), accepting ambiguity risk
questions.explanation: Single direction is the safe default; 'both' is for specific reverse-filter needs and adds ambiguity risk.

questions.question: Which DAX function performs context transition (row → filter context)?
questions.explanation: CALCULATE transitions the current row context into an equivalent filter context.

questions.question: Which pre-attentive attribute encodes value most accurately?
questions.explanation: Position is the strongest pre-attentive channel; area and hue are far weaker for precise comparison.

questions.question: Why avoid a pie chart with 12 slices?
options: Humans can't accurately compare many angular areas — use a sorted bar chart
Power BI can't render more than 8 slices
Pies are only for time series
questions.explanation: Many-slice pies are unreadable; a sorted horizontal bar chart compares far better.

questions.question: For a bar chart, where must the value axis start?
questions.explanation: Bars encode magnitude by length from zero; truncating the axis exaggerates differences.

questions.question: What is progressive disclosure in a dashboard?
options: Showing every metric on one page
Overview first, then detail on demand via drill-through, tooltips, and bookmarks
questions.explanation: Progressive disclosure manages cognitive load: reveal detail only when the user asks for it.

questions.question: Which Power BI feature jumps from a data point to a detail page pre-filtered to that context?
questions.explanation: Drill-through pages open a detail page filtered to the right-clicked context.

questions.question: Which function gives a clean YoY comparison by shifting the date range back one year?
questions.explanation: SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR (a DATEADD shortcut) shifts the current range back exactly one year.

questions.question: What distinguishes a KPI from a plain metric?
options: A KPI must be a percentage
A KPI has a target and a threshold that drives a decision
A KPI is always shown as a card
A KPI cannot use time intelligence
questions.explanation: A KPI = metric + target + threshold that prompts an action; 'Revenue' alone is just a metric.

questions.question: Which pattern gives readable multi-condition RAG status logic?
questions.explanation: SWITCH(TRUE(), …) reads as a clean top-to-bottom condition ladder for RAG thresholds.

questions.question: For dynamic RLS, which function identifies the signed-in user?
questions.explanation: USERPRINCIPALNAME() returns the UPN to match against a user→scope security table.

questions.question: What problem do calculation groups solve?
options: They apply reusable time-intelligence (YTD/PY/YoY) to any measure without duplicating logic
questions.explanation: Calculation groups define time-intelligence once and apply it to any measure via a slicer.

questions.question: What is the right way to distribute a report to 50+ read-only consumers?
options: Publish a Power BI App built from the workspace
Give everyone Admin on the workspace
questions.explanation: Apps are curated, read-only, versioned distribution; sharing the workspace exposes dev artifacts.

questions.question: What must the source support for incremental refresh to work well?
options: Query folding on the date filter
questions.explanation: Incremental refresh relies on query folding so the date-range filter is pushed to the source.

questions.question: In DAX Studio, SE time dominates a slow query. What does that indicate?
options: The DAX formula is too complex (Formula Engine bound)
The query is data-scan bound (Storage Engine) — reduce volume/cardinality or add aggregations
questions.explanation: SE = Storage Engine (data scanning); FE = Formula Engine (DAX complexity). SE-bound means reduce data work.

questions.question: What is the single highest-leverage way to shrink a model?
questions.explanation: Every column costs memory and refresh time; removing unused high-cardinality columns is the top win.

questions.question: When might AWS QuickSight fit better than Power BI?
options: For an AWS-native serverless stack with per-session pricing at large, occasional-use viewer counts
When you need DAX calculation groups
When you need the VertiPaq engine
questions.explanation: QuickSight suits AWS-native, serverless, pay-per-session scenarios; Power BI suits the Microsoft + DAX stack.

questions.question: What are the first two steps of the domain immersion protocol?
options: Read the business context, then inventory the data (tables, grain, dirtiness)
Pick a theme, then add filters
questions.explanation: You orient before you build: understand audience/decisions, then inventory the data.

questions.question: What is the '80/20 dashboard' heuristic?
options: A few KPI cards plus a couple of trend charts answer most executive questions — build those first
questions.explanation: The first KPI cards and trends answer the bulk of exec questions; build them before the long tail.

questions.question: You're 3 hours in with no working end-to-end flow. What went wrong?
options: You over-invested in polish before shipping a working model→measures→visuals→publish path
questions.explanation: Ship-then-polish: get the whole path working first, then improve design and edge cases.

questions.question: Under time pressure, what do you keep and what do you cut?
options: Keep extra pages; cut the data model
Keep a correct model + core KPIs + one clean exec page published; cut extra pages and cosmetic polish
Cut time intelligence to save time
questions.explanation: Correctness and the core exec view are non-negotiable; the long tail and polish are the first to go.

questions.question: Why is rapid domain adaptation the skill being tested on capstone day?
options: Because real BI work means absorbing an unfamiliar domain and delivering under ambiguity and time pressure
Because it removes the need for stakeholders
questions.explanation: The capstone simulates the real job: a new domain, a deadline, and a production-quality deliverable.

questions.question: How should the 5-minute business-context pitch open?
options: With the data sources and refresh schedule
With the 'so what' — business impact and the decision the dashboard enables
With a tour of every DAX measure
With the tool version and licensing
questions.explanation: Lead with impact and the decision enabled; technology comes later in the walkthrough.

questions.question: In hostile Q&A, what is the strongest response when you don't know?
options: "I don't know — here's how I'd find out", then outline the approach
questions.explanation: Panels reward honest reasoning and a method over bluffing.

questions.question: A VP says the number is wrong. What's the right first move?
options: Reproduce it, then check the filter context / slicers before anything else
questions.explanation: Systematic debugging starts by reproducing and inspecting the filter context — the usual culprit.

questions.question: What signals Lead / Analytics Manager level in the defense?
options: Only that the DAX is correct
Flexing register from exec pitch to technical deep-dive to stakeholder management in one session
questions.explanation: Senior calibration comes from communication range and reasoning, not just correct calculations.

questions.question: What is the final recruitment artifact produced on Day 7?
options: A seniority calibration note (level + the one thing that moves you up)
questions.explanation: The calibration note (with rubric scores and the recording) is the recruitment output.
